imp.generic: The Santa Ana winds make people uneasy.
imp.author: The wind shows us how close to the edge we are. I have lived in the West a long time, and I have come to know that the Santa Ana, blowing in from the desert, lays a passive, malevolent unease over everything.

imp.generic: In 1968 I was going through a difficult period.
imp.author: This was a year when I did not believe in the narrative and did not want to. It was 1968, the year I went out to look at California and could not stop noticing the way the light came down flat over the freeways.

imp.generic: Los Angeles felt strange and threatening that summer.
imp.author: It was the season of suicide and divorce and prickly dread, wherever the wind blew. I remember it was 105 degrees in Pasadena and nobody was talking about anything but the heat and the children gone missing.

imp.generic: She wore a nice dress to her wedding.
imp.author: She was married in a peau de soie dress the color of café au lait, in a chapel off the Strip, at midnight, for $35, and she believed she was beginning something.

imp.generic: People in this town pursue unrealistic dreams.
imp.author: This is a place where people come to lose the bad memories, or to find the new life, and where the freeway signs name towns that are mostly the idea of a town. I am talking here about the will to believe.

imp.generic: After that, things changed for me.
imp.author: I tell you this not to enlist your sympathy but because it is the only way I know to begin: after that, the center did not hold, and I stopped pretending it had.

imp.generic: The motel was cheap and run-down.
imp.author: The motel was the kind with a swimming pool drained for the season and a sign that said VACANCY in a color of pink that had stopped meaning welcome some years before.

imp.generic: Grief is a complicated emotion that takes time to process.
imp.author: Grief turns out to be a place none of us know until we reach it. We do not expect the moment to keep coming back, the unexpected need to give away the shoes, the way the mind circles the one fact it cannot keep.

imp.generic: I learned an important lesson from the experience.
imp.author: I learned what I could from it, which was less than I had wanted and not the thing I had gone looking for. I learned that the story I told myself was the story I needed, not the story that was true.

imp.generic: The hot weather continued for several days.
imp.author: The heat held. It held through Tuesday and into the long flat afternoons, and by Thursday the whole valley had the bleached, expectant look of a place waiting for something it would not name.
